svg.title: For a finite signed combination w = (wt), put Λwf = P t wtf(t). If |P t wt(t/R)n| ≤η for every n, absolute convergence gives ∥Λwf∥≤ηA. This estimate uses cancellation of the combination; replacing wt by |wt| would lose it. Products preserve (ASP1) with the product allowance, by the absolutely summable Cauchy product. Summable families preserve it by the double-series theorem. Exponentiation gives allowance eA−1 for ef −1, by summing the positive scalar majorant P q≥1Aq/q!.
